title: SLO-headroom-gated active-active cutover with streaming resume and circuit hysteresis
creator: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: Hosted API edge cutovers for active-active regions must avoid user-visible dropped streams and SLO regressions. Current cutover mechanisms drain at host-level which causes increased tail latency and stream resets when traffic is shifted during congestion. This ticket designs and implements a cutover protocol gated by SLO headroom and circuit hysteresis, combined with a streaming-resume token handshake and probabilistic load-shedding fallback so that we preserve session continuity where possible and degrade gracefully when necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled active-active cutover that reduces stream resets vs today by >= 80% in load tests
No production SLO (p99 latency, success rate) regression greater than 5% during normal canary traffic shifts
Circuit hysteresis prevents flip-flop at region boundaries during oscillating load patterns
Streaming resume tokens accepted by downstream proxies and result in resumed KV prefix lookups without user-visible duplication
Load-shedding policy triggers only when headroom < configured threshold and follows probabilistic policy documented below
notes: High level plan: implement SLO headroom monitor in gateway, extend traffic-shifter to accept gating signal, add streaming-resume handshake (resume_token exchange + earliest-allowed-offset), instrument circuit breaker hysteresis state machine (open, probing, closed) and implement probabilistic token-based shedding in egress path.
SLO headroom calculation: headroom = max(0, (target_p99_latency - current_p99_latency) / target_p99_latency). Use a 30s sliding window and expo smoothing (alpha=0.2) to prevent transient flips.
Gating thresholds: open gating when headroom < 0.15 for > 45s; force broker-level shedding when headroom < 0.05 for > 30s. These thresholds will be configurable per-customer/tier.
Circuit hysteresis: after circuit opens for region A, require headroom > 0.25 for 60s before allowing traffic to reintroduce; probing phase ramps at 2% of connection rates to validate stability.

Streaming-resume handshake: producer attaches resume_token and last_seq_id in a per-connection metadata header when shifting; consumer proxies must accept a resume_token within a 5s grace window and perform KV prefix cache warmup for that session id. If resume fails, fall back to new session creation with user-visible reconnect guidance in SDK.

Probabilistic shedding: when triggered, compute shed_probability = clamp((0.15 - headroom) / 0.15, 0, 1). Apply per-tenant deterministic hashing by request id with randomization seed tied to epoch to avoid correlated shedding, so a given session is either consistently shed or kept during short windows.

Observability: add metrics: region_headroom, region_circuit_state, resume_success_rate, shed_probability_applied, shed_rate_by_tier, stream_reset_rate. Add tracing spans for handshake and cutover decisions with tags: gating_reason, probe_fraction.

Compatibility: ensure existing short-poll (non-stream) paths work unchanged. Streaming clients using earlier SDKs will receive resume-failure and reconnect; document behavior in SDK changelog and release notes.

Rollout: staged rollout — internal testbed -> canary customers (5%) -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%. Each stage gated by SLO and resume_success_rate metrics. Automated rollback if p99 latency or error rate crosses configured safety thresholds.
Backward-compat: grace period of 30 days for resume handshake before strict enforcement; proxies must accept both resume and legacy headers for the period.
Security: resume_token is ephemeral and signed (HMAC with edge key). Tokens rotate weekly. Security review required for token format disclosure and KMS usage.
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created. Design sketched during reliability guild sync. Assigned to Luis for implementation plan.
2025-02-18: Spike completed — measured headroom smoothing parameters on staging traffic: alpha=0.2 and 30s window gave stable signal with fewer false positives than 10s window.
2025-02-25: Implemented gate eval logic and circuit state machine in gateway; added unit tests for hysteresis transitions and headroom calc.
2025-02-28: End-to-end integration test run against synthetic multi-region load. Observed 72% reduction in stream resets compared to naive drain; probe fraction tuning pending.
2025-03-03: Canary plan approved by SRE and Product. Added tracing spans and dashboards for region_headroom and resume_success_rate before canary. Scheduled canary for 2025-03-06.

2025-03-04: Discovered resume_token signing library mismatch between old proxy and new edge with rotation enabled. Hotfix PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/edge/PR-4879. Will patch proxies in canary region prior to shift.
